messages:
incident-bot: P0 ALERT: tenant-level KV/prefix cache hit-rate collapse detected for tenant cust-alpha (dedicated-eu1). Conditions: tenant_hit_rate < 5% for 10m, eviction_rate > 80k/10m, pool_mem_pressure > 90%. Paging on-call.
harper: I'm on-call. Pulling up dashboards. seeing hit-rate ~2.1% and eviction spikes aligned with traffic surge about 18:02 UTC. p95 latency increased ~900ms.
sam: Looking at runtime logs, lots of unique prefix keys being inserted. Many look like client-side trace IDs appended to prefixes: e.g. "ctx:trace:abcd-1234-user:payload". That will shard the cache.
nina: Is this tenant in a VPC/dedicated flow? could be an integration change.
harper: Yes, cust-alpha is on dedicated-eu1 (VPC). We need to treat isolation carefully, customers can't be routed off-prem without consent.
cse_lee: I reached out to the customer's integration lead. They confirmed a client rollout today that included per-request debug IDs in the prompt prefix. They can rollback, but want Redwood to propose a mitigation before they flip.
ina: Short term mitigations we can do without customer action:
- 1) Apply prefix canonicalization at our edge proxy to strip known debug-id patterns (best effort)
- 2) Temporarily lower tenant cache quota and increase eviction aggressiveness for cust-alpha
- 3) Soft-disable tenant KV cache (safe, but increases cost/latency)
- 4) Background eviction of low-hit long-lived prefixes

sam: We can push a proxy rewrite rule quickly. Example nginx lua snippet (very rough):
```
-- strip debug id suffixes matching [-|:]debug-[a-f0-9]{8}
local key = ngx.var.prefix
local cleaned = ngx.re.gsub(key, "[-:]debug-[a-f0-9]{8}$", "")
ngx.var.proxy_key = cleaned
```
This will canonicalize a large fraction of the junk keys.

harper: I like a two-step approach: 1) push proxy canonicalization as hotfix, 2) run a targeted eviction and reduce tenant quota. If the proxy fails to reduce new unique-prefix-rate we disable cache.

sre-bot: metrics dump: "kv_cache.hit_rate{tenant=\"cust-alpha\"}=2.1%", "kv_cache.evictions{tenant=\"cust-alpha\"}=96k", "kv_cache.items{tenant=\"cust-alpha\"}=4.3M", pool_mem_pressure=93% (dedicated-eu1) (last 5m)

sam: I'll stage the proxy rewrite to the dedicated-eu1 ingress points. pushing now to canary nodes.

nina: While that deploys, let's prepare the admin commands if we need to change tenant settings.

Example API call to reduce quota:
```
PATCH /admin/tenants/cust-alpha
{ "kv_cache": { "max_items": 500000, "eviction_policy": "aggressive" } }
```
To disable cache entirely:
```
PATCH /admin/tenants/cust-alpha
{ "kv_cache": { "enabled": false } }
```

incident-bot: DEPLOY START: proxy-canonicalize-cust-alpha -> canary (3 hosts)
sam: Canary looks good; new metrics show unique-prefix-rate drop ~68% on canaries. Preparing to roll to remaining ingress nodes.

cse_lee: Customer ready to pause if we recommend; they prefer we try the canonicalization first and hold rollback unless necessary.
harper: Rolling patch to all ingress nodes now.

sre-bot: Post-roll metrics: unique-prefix-rate for cust-alpha dropped 85% overall. Eviction rate dropping. mem_pressure -> 76%.

nina: Great. Now run a background eviction job for the longest-lived low-hit prefixes to free up memory faster. Sam, can you run the eviction with pattern matching TTL < 5m AND hit_count == 1? We don't want to evict useful items.
sam: Running eviction job: `POST /admin/kv/evict` payload: `{ "tenant": "cust-alpha", "filter": "ttl<300 AND hits<=1" }` -> estimated 2.6M entries removed.

sre-bot: Eviction complete. pool_mem_pressure -> 58%. kv_cache.hit_rate climbing toward 22% as client traffic normalizes.

pm_raul: Customer-facing note: customer (cust-alpha) reported degraded p95 for ~17 minutes. They appreciate the rapid mitigation. Will draft a short incident summary for their account.
cse_lee: Customer confirmed they will stop shipping debug IDs in future releases and will add an allowlisted prefix field so we can cache safely.

harper: Next operational steps:
- Keep the canonicalization in place at the ingress for 24h
- Add alerting for unique-prefix-rate > 5k/min for dedicated pools
- Implement per-tenant unique-prefix-rate throttle to prevent replays
- Add validation to the tenant onboarding flow that warns about high-cardinality prefix usage

nina: Long-term engineering changes:
- Proxy-level canonicalization rules (configurable per-tenant)
- Per-tenant prefix admission control + rate-limiter
- Reduce default TTL for prefixes with low hit counts
- Dashboard showing unique-prefix churn per tenant

sam: I'll file INF-4512 to track the proxy rule hardening and INF-4513 for runtime admission control.

harper: Incident state -> mitigated. customer impacted: increased latency p95 for 17m. Root cause: client rollout that appended per-request debug IDs to prompt prefixes causing cache pollution and eviction storm. Remediation: proxy canonicalization, targeted eviction, quota reduction; long-term followups assigned.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: state=mitigated, duration=00:28:00, actions=[proxy_canonicalize, eviction, quota_reduce], impact=customer_degraded_p95, notes=\"tenant remained available, higher token-cost briefly\"

harper: Adding handoff notes for night on-call. I'm tagging sam and nina for followups. Leaving for @sam in 30m. Thanks team. :coffee:
